verdict: Revenue jumped 36% because Regeneron's share of Dupixent profits from Sanofi stepped up sharply once the Sanofi development balance was fully repaid.

kpis.label: Collaboration revenue
kpis.note: +52% YoY, mostly the Sanofi profit share

segments.name: Collaboration revenue
segments.note: Regeneron's share of profits from medicines sold by partners, mainly Dupixent sold by Sanofi.

segments.name: Net product sales
segments.note: Medicines Regeneron sells itself, including EYLEA HD and Libtayo.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Other contract and program revenue, including government-related work.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Finding and testing new medicines; includes $22M of acquired in-process research and development (buying early-stage research from others).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling medicines and running the company.

takeaways.title: Revenue surged to $5.12B
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 36% from a year earlier to $5.12B, driven by a much bigger profit share from the Sanofi partnership.

takeaways.title: Collaboration money is now the biggest stream
takeaways.text: Collaboration revenue was $3.00B, up 52%. Sanofi sells Dupixent and Regeneron keeps a share of the profit; that share rose after the development balance was repaid in full last quarter.

takeaways.title: Profit rose to $1.95B
takeaways.text: Net income was $1.95B, up 33% from a year earlier, even though research spending rose 22% to $1.79B.

footerNote: Cost of revenue combines cost of goods sold ($322M) and cost of collaboration and contract manufacturing ($252M), the two product-cost lines in the release. The research and development line includes acquired in-process research and development of $22M. Other income of $236M is other income, net ($247M) minus interest expense ($11M), rounded to whole millions.
